The procedure took three days. We didn't even think he was going to make it after enduring that much blood loss, but when he woke up...his blood ran blue. The crimson ember that ran through his veins like magma, now icy and cold. Gaheron is probably moving mountains in the Mists out of spite.  
  
I'm scared. What are we doing here? Vastya is already looking for more candidates, and I will not be first in line.

strings.en:
*Gardesano's account as transcribed by Amanuensis Nofra*  
  
I have made a breakthrough with my newest pupils. Some of my fellow docents at the primary conservatoire had their misgivings, among those outside these halls, but what good is the experience of a proper education without space to pursue one's fancies, one's passions? The mursaat we admit to study in Stellis Quor should come to know Tyria as we do, its power, its beauty, and its dangers, within reason. But I digress. Last week's lessons were something of a personal interest to me.  
  
In recent days, both Elka and Antenor have taken a growing interest in my stewards, and so I offered to instruct them in the delicate craft of shaping and enchanting their own arcano-constructs. Even with these rudimentary lessons and my limited facilities in the city, Elka was able to follow my methods to the letter as if she were my very shadow. And she produced an impressive first attempt, a near-perfect simulacrum of one of my own stewards with some noticeable differences in flair.   
  
Antenor... Well, he took a direct approach. He asked if he could supply his own materials and returned the following day with several large violet jadestones; an inspired choice, I thought. Jade has shown potential in the use of arcane constructs, but for reasons I've yet to discern, it's a material that takes greater arcane input to reach a functional baseline than other materials I've experimented with, and I tend to lean toward efficiency. But he was diligent, insouciant; it took Antenor much longer than Elka to finish his first construct, but it paid off. The small thing was even able to hover with the best of us.   
  
I still smile when I think about their work, the potential their newfound crafts could provide for them and their people. It will be the honor of a lifetime to watch and see what becomes of their studies and their contributions to the mursaat. Such is the near unique pride of a teacher. I suppose it will have to suffice, in absence of their elder relations.

strings.en:
Waiting Sorrow has left us. She left a note—she left Dagda a note. "I must be swift, should Isgarren catch on to my plan before I'm able to depart." What am I? A creature of nightmare? Do they writhe when I speak? Do they flee when I move?  
  
The court is quiet today. Dagda fled to the observatory. Mabon is disappointed with my reaction. Perhaps screaming until I opened a portal to the Domain of Anguish was a tad ostentatious.  
  
The emotion that lingers at the pit of my stomach is repentance, mostly. Sorrow is simply a harbinger of my prior mistakes. My negligence. When she came to me—goodness knows, well before the gods doomed this place—I saw someone struggling, and I chose to help her. A Voice on the verge of Koda's rage; who knows what she would've done had I not ascended her and severed that connection? Sidony never thought of me the same after that. I imagine my saving Sorrow was the final straw before exile.  
  
I've often thought of my choice as naïve, and at other times I've wondered if the elder races were too protective of magic. But I turned her immortal—I gave her access to immense power to save her life. That shouldn't have been my choice.   
  
I let her roam on her own for a long, long time before she and Vass joined us. And when I saw how powerful she'd become... I couldn't let her go again. She knows this. She's grown more and more unpredictable over the centuries. She even claims to see "flickers" of her life before ascension. When the kodan split between Janthir and Orr, I could tell it bothered her—I could tell she yearned to help her people when they were clearly splitting apart. But she's a figure of fable now to them. What if she were to reveal herself as the missing Voice to their ancestral Claw? The Claw that determined the fate of all kodan when he moved them to safety? She'd cause riots... They're already fragile enough.
  
I need time to think about my next steps.

strings.en: Notes: Made hands tingle a little. Exciting!

As I linger on these shores, I wonder... How many of my kind will see their dreams to fruition? How many fledglings are doomed to wilt before their dreams are realized? Standing here now, I pity those that will never fulfill their own. How I once thought I would never see mine complete, or even understand what it meant...  
  
In my dream I was walking, barefoot, across an empty, ethereal beach. The air made me feel alive in a way that I would soon yearn for after waking. As I moved my hands across the foliage and through the sands, my fingers tingled with power... I can hardly explain the feeling and still sound sensible. I felt greeted by an unknowable force. Eventually, strange murmurs beckoned me inland, and I walked until I was beneath a thick forest canopy. In this forest, magic clung to the air. It was everywhere! And it was somehow more primal than anything I would come to know in the Grove or Caledon.  
  
While my own existence had only just begun, or was beginning, I somehow knew that I was young and that this place was very old. I followed the old magic and the whispers, and I walked, and walked, and walked, for what felt like days, until I finally reached that place. A sacred ground, where all the magic on this strange island culminated. And then I opened my eyes for the first time, and everything around me was duller in comparison. I was born hungry, but disappointed.  
  
I looked across the ocean and knew that the land I stood on was not the place that I witnessed in my dream. It was like there was a string tied to that beach, and that string spooled across the ocean and connected to my chest. I could always feel it, but its pull was very faint. I knew it was real and that it breathed, but I also knew it was very far away. With every tug I felt, yearning burned brighter in my core.  
  
It wasn't until long that I found others who'd experienced the same Dream of Dreams. We all felt that ache pulling us toward the ocean, under the canopy, and to that place. Unfulfilled by "home" in the Grove, with Mother's blessing we decided to venture to Lion's Arch to see if we could find a ship. Unfortunately our kin were so fresh to the world that most feared allowing us aboard. The ship captain's cited bad luck, or worries of Zhaitan's corrosive blight. So...I became a captain myself. Captain Bidelia.  
   
Years of bartering for a vessel, learning to sail, and building out our crew... We found a few more daring souls that weren't afraid of the Elder Dragon's hold over the seas, and we set sail at last. That pull my brothers and sisters and I all felt grew louder and stronger as we pushed against the tides. Our excitement blossomed. The impossible felt possible, at last... That is, until the storms. And then we reached the fog. And then we struck that damned rock. And so many dreams were suddenly unfulfilled...  
    
What few of us survived clung to the scraps of our ship, with no perception that we'd survive the hour. We clung to each other as the sun set and thick, cold air rippled over the ocean. But when I woke, what I felt... We made it.  
  
We're here. Stuck, but nonetheless...here.

Hai Jii stood before the dais where Grenth sat, and he begged, "Please, this isn't their fault. I'm the one that killed the invaders—my hands are dipped in their blood."

The God of Death pondered the boy's pleas; but instead of showing any benevolence, he sentenced Hai Jii's family to an eternity of torture by flame. The boy crumpled to the floor and wept tears of magma. His cheeks burned away with every drop.

When he awoke, his body was made of stars—his arms powerful, fiery wings. A new phoenix had risen from the ashes of the Underworld, and he took his throne beside the other Celestials. There, he would weep an eternity of flame.

In what is more colloquially known as the "Pantless Incident of '04," norn hunter Sven Liefson risked greatly damaging norn/human relations with irresponsible consumption of drink. After several rounds, a visibly intoxicated Liefson challenged a nearby human to a test of strength. When the human settler repeatedly declined his challenge, Liefson mocked him, going as far to remove his pants and shake his behind in the human's face. This incident serves as an excellent teaching moment for key faux pas to avoid in interspecies communications. After sobering up a few days later, Liefson apologized to the human in question. The two are said to have become great friends following the debacle.
